LISTENING GUIDE / 16 TRACKS

Korean indie: where to start

Some songs, live performances and a little about the people behind them. A place to start if Korean music is new to you.

BY INDIEK / PUBLISHED 2026-10-19 / UPDATED 2026-10-21

Follow via RSS ↗

There’s a love song by The Black Skirts, a farewell from YdBB and a live version of SE SO NEON’s The Wave that carries on long after the singing ends. You can dip in wherever you like.

You don’t need to know Korean to spend time here. Yerin Baek’s 0310 is sung in English, and each song’s artist page has English notes on the meaning and mood of its lyrics. More artists appear below, with new additions as the journal grows.

  1. 01

    The Black Skirts / 검정치마

    EVERYTHING

    The Black Skirts is Bryan Cho’s solo project. EVERYTHING is a love song that first came out in 2016, before joining the album TEAM BABY a year later. The official music video is here, and the album is linked on his artist page if you’d like more.

    Official music videoListen & read ↗

    Behind the song. Bryan Cho was born in Seoul and grew up in New Jersey. He also goes by the Korean name Jo Hyu-il.

    You might also like: Kim Sawol / Someone. A folk song that holds affection and doubt together.

    Inside the lyrics ↗
  2. 02

    Yerin Baek / 백예린

    0310

    0310 is sung in English, with lyrics on screen in Yerin Baek’s own video. It comes from Every letter I sent you., an album she describes as a collection of thoughts and memories from ages nineteen to twenty-three. Square (2017) is another song from the same record.

    Official lyric videoListen & read ↗

    Behind the song. The recording has acoustic guitar, strings and a full band behind Baek’s voice. Those details sit alongside the personal memories she describes in the album notes.

    You might also like: Choi Yu Ree / Forest. A live folk session, with a song about finding a place among others.

    Inside the lyrics ↗
  3. 03

    YdBB / 유다빈밴드

    ONCE

    YdBB are a five-piece band built around singer-songwriter Yu Dabin, playing music that moves between acoustic folk and rock. ONCE is about letting someone go while hoping they’ll remember you kindly. It’s a farewell she talks about in the band’s release interview.

    Official audioListen & read ↗

    Behind the song. Yu Dabin made the cover by drawing over a photograph of her own hand. She left the thing held inside unnamed, so listeners could bring their own meaning to it.

    You might also like: WhiteUsedSocks / Don’t feel sad. Another band to spend time with, and a song from their early days.

    Inside the lyrics ↗
  4. 04

    HANRORO / 한로로

    Even if you leave

    In Even if you leave, HANRORO writes about the things that are hard to let go of. Her release note describes being caught between blaming someone else and blaming yourself, and trying to get through the day without making that feeling worse.

    Official audioListen & read ↗

    Behind the song. The song needn’t be about an ex. In her note, HANRORO also writes about a choice, a neglected relationship or something that traps you in your own thinking. It followed her 2022 debut, Let Me Love My Youth.

    You might also like: Motte / Don’t run away. Another song about a relationship, from the A-TEEN soundtrack.

    Inside the lyrics ↗
  5. 05

    SE SO NEON / 새소년

    The Wave

    Hwang Soyoon’s voice and guitar are at the centre of SE SO NEON’s The Wave. This version was filmed at the 2020/NEON concert in December 2019. After the last vocal line, the performance carries on with a long instrumental ending.

    Live performanceListen & read ↗

    Behind the song. The Wave was released in 2017 and appeared on Summer Plumage that year. It won Best Rock Song at the 2018 Korean Music Awards.

    You might also like: ESEGYE / RomanceYouthLove. ESEGYE at their first BLIND concert, filmed at Veloso Hongdae.

    Inside the lyrics ↗
